title: SideQuest: choose the visual world
question: The roll landed on Ready Check: the guild site built from the raid interface every WoW player reads on raid night. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Ready Check
options.lineage: The raid UI on raid night: raid frames, ready check, pull timers, class and item-quality colors
options.thesis: The site is the guild's raid interface, and the first thing it does is ask you to click Ready.
materials: translucent tooltip panels with a fine double border
raid-frame health bars in class colors
options.viewport: A real ready-check dialog ('SideQuest has initiated a ready check') as the hero CTA: Ready opens the Discord, Not Ready scrolls down to learn more. Behind it, a 40-slot raid frame grid with nearly every slot an open, designed ghost frame. A live pull-timer bar drains toward the Nov 4 launch. A giant raid-warning headline sits over it all.
options.risk: It's the tool the audience already uses, so it could read as a costume or as sweaty. Dark ground sits near the 'near-black + neon' rut; item-quality colors have to carry it.

raised.raise: Unlit is designed too: open raid slots are drawn as deliberately as filled ones, and that is how we recruit.
Color stays on edges and names (frame borders, item titles, chat channels). Body text stays achromatic, the way tooltips work.
One fixed-scale raid grid persists down the page, and its fill-state tells the guild's timeline: forming, launch, dungeons, Molten Core.
Raid-warning text at monumental scale is the headline voice, never a timid H1.
Density courage: raid charts and signups use real tabular density instead of a card grid.
One trajectory: the launch pull-timer bar is the page's single motion vector, and every later timer rides the same track.

options.label: The Official Strategy Guide
options.lineage: The 2004 printed WoW strategy guide: glossy spreads, numbered boss maps, loot tables, Tip sidebars
options.thesis: SideQuest as a chapter in the guidebook every veteran owned: the guild documented like a dungeon.
options.viewport: An open guide spread: left page 'Chapter: SideQuest' with a numbered callout map (1 = Discord, 2 = raids, 3 = addons). Right page has a 'Recommended level / group size / rewards' stat box with Join Discord as the reward, and a Tip sidebar.
options.risk: My top-ranked candidate, and the familiar one. Print spreads can drift toward editorial-magazine habits, and it resonates most with veterans.

options.label: Seasonal Folio
options.lineage: botanical folio of one subject across fixed-scale stages
options.thesis: One character drawn at levels 1, 20, 40, and 60 on one baseline.
options.viewport: Four fixed-scale plates of a hero leveling up, captions beneath.
options.case: Fuses onto the journey, but players don't recognize the form, and it never shows raids, addons, or signups.
options.risk: Cream plate ground: a known rut, and quiet for a guild.
options.kept: Fixed-scale sequence: the raid grid keeps one scale while its fill-state tells the timeline.

options.label: Pulp Plate
options.thesis: A gryphon crossing a red sky on a diagonal, its title lettered at speed.
options.viewport: Diagonal flight plate with the guild name in streamlined caps.
options.case: Spectacle without guild function. Loses on recognition and on clarity.
options.risk: Becomes a painted poster with no working parts.
options.kept: One trajectory: the launch timer is the page's single motion vector.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: Achromatic field, spectral color only at the edges.
options.viewport: White field, guild name ringed by a thin spectral fringe.
options.case: No WoW identity at all. Loses on both axes.
options.kept: Color lives only on edges and names. Body text stays neutral.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Floating combat text as matter: words that hit, crit, and scatter.
options.viewport: SIDEQUEST bursts into scrolling combat text across white.
options.case: Clever, but it never shows how the guild works.
options.kept: Monumental type: the raid-warning headline at full scale.

options.label: Segment Display
options.thesis: Launch countdown as a scoreboard, ghost segments and all.
options.viewport: Giant red countdown digits with Join below.
options.case: A strong countdown, but it isn't Azeroth. Loses on recognition and on clarity.
options.kept: Unlit is designed: empty raid slots are drawn as deliberately as filled ones.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The combat log as a black-and-white data sublime.
options.viewport: Strobing log columns with the guild name inverted.
options.case: Cold. Casual members won't see themselves in it.
options.risk: Feels like a parse site, the 'too sweaty' failure.
options.kept: Density courage in raid charts and signups.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The classic guild site, built to a high standard: cinematic hero, crest, schedule, recruitment, Join.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed atmospheric art, centered crest and guild name, Join Discord button, then About / Raids / Recruitment sections.
canonCard.risk: This is the generic fantasy-MMO template you asked to avoid, and it needs key art we don't have.
